titulo_es: Choose according to the subject of the subordinate

soprattutto.consejo: A warning of enhancement and preference.

bloques.titulo: The golden rule of the verbal economy
texto: **Mismo sujeto**: The speaker performs both actions. It is linked with preposition + infinitive: **Spero di partire** (I hope to leave), **Penso di avere ragione** (I think I am right), **Vorrei restare** (I would like to stay). «spero che io parta» sounds unnatural in Italian.
**Distinto sujeto**: two different people are involved. It links with **che + congiuntivo**: **Spero che tu parta** (I hope you go out), **Vorrei che tu restassi** (I want you to stay).

filas: Penso che tu sappia la verità.
Voglio che tu compri una casa.

frases.it: Spero di partire presto per le vacanze. Ho davvero bisogno di riposo.
frases.es: Espero salir pronto de vacaciones. Tengo de verdad necesidad de descanso.
frases.en: I hope to be on vacation soon. I really need a break.

frases.it: Anch'io vorrei riposarmi, ma spero soprattutto che il capo mi conceda i giorni richiesti.
frases.es: Yo también quisiera descansar, pero espero sobre todo que el jefe me conceda los días solicitados.
frases.en: I would also like to rest, but I hope, above all, that the boss will grant me the days requested.
analisis: But I hope most of all

frases.it: Se vuoi, posso aiutarti a finire il lavoro prima di venerdì.
frases.es: Si quieres, puedo ayudarte a terminar el trabajo antes del viernes.
frases.en: If you want, I can help you finish the job by Friday.
analisis: posso aiutarti a finire il lavoro
I can help you finish the job.

frases.it: Grazie mille, sei gentilissimo! Speriamo di finire tutto in tempo.
frases.es: ¡Muchas gracias, eres amabilísimo! Esperemos terminar todo a tiempo.
frases.en: Thank you very much, you are so amabilous! Let's hope we finish it all in time.
analisis: speriamo di finire tutto in tempo
Let's hope to finish it all in time.

bloques.pregunta: Why does Valerio say «Spero di partire» instead of «Spero che io parta»?

opciones.texto: Because the subject of hope and exit is the same person (Valerio).
opciones.explicacion: When the subjects agree, the use of + infinitive preposition is required.

opciones.texto: Because the verb «partire» has no conjugation in congiuntive.
opciones.explicacion: «Partire» is regularly conjugated in all modes.

opciones.texto: Because travel on vacation always requires the use of infinitive.
opciones.explicacion: It is a syntactic rule of correference of grammatical subjects.

bloques.frase: Chiara spera che il suo capo le ___ le ferie la settimana prossima.

opciones.explicacion: Different subjects (Chiara waits / the boss grants): che + congiuntivo present.
It is present of indicative: fact accomplished.
The infinitive cannot carry a different lexic subject interposed.

bloques.pregunta: Who are the subjects of this prayer?
bloques.frase: Speriamo di finire tutto in tempo per le vacanze.

opciones.texto: The subject of both verbs is us (noi): we wait and we finish.
opciones.explicacion: Same subject in both actions: «di + infinitive» is used.

opciones.texto: The subject of waiting is us and the one of finishing is the director of the company.
opciones.explicacion: If they were different, it would be «speriamo che il direttore finisca».

opciones.texto: The subject is impersonal and does not refer to any team member.
opciones.explicacion: It corresponds to the first person of the plural (noi).

bloques.frase: Spero di finire questo lavoro prima di partire per il mare
bloques.traduccion: I hope to finish this job before I go out to the sea.
bloques.explicacion: Double infinitive with the same subject in both subordinate clauses.

bloques.pregunta: How would you formulate «I want you to study more.» (different subjects)?

opciones.texto: Voglio che tu studi di più.
opciones.explicacion: Different subjects: verb «volere» + che + congiuntivo de studiare.
It means «I want to study more.» (same subject).

opciones.texto: Voglio che tu studiare di più.
opciones.explicacion: It is an agrimatic construction in Italian.

bloques.frase: Luca pensa di avere ___ tempo per completare il progetto.

opciones.explicacion: Unchanging warning or adjective of sufficient amount.
Little would express a shortage opposed to the positive sense.

bloques.pregunta: Why can't you use infinitive here?
bloques.frase: Vorrei che tu mi ascoltassi quando ti parlo.

opciones.texto: Because the desire is part of «I», but the action of listening falls to «You».
opciones.explicacion: The divergence of people requires subordinate introduced by «che».

opciones.texto: Because the infinitive is only used in interrogative phrases.
opciones.explicacion: The infinitive is used in any type of sentence with matching subjects.

opciones.texto: Because «ascoltare» is a direct transitory verb.
opciones.explicacion: The transitivity does not influence the alternation between infinitive and congiuntive.

intro: A very common error at intermediate levels is to use «che + congiuntivo» when the two subjects match. Remember: in Italian, if you don't change your subject, you must use infinitive.
